baseline_measured.instrument: `larql vindex3 ops <container> --realizations [--budget-gib N]` (this worktree): plans, opens the store from segment headers only, runs `select_realizations` under the production CPU backend and `ExecutionSlice::Full`, prices the pins with `expectations` from the tensor tables, and holds the working set against the budget. No payload byte is read (93 MB RSS over a 98 GB container). Cost 84 s wall (26 s user, 40 s sys) — an instrument fact, recorded, not the subject.

BF16 → cpu:decode-f32+BlasF32 (size poli.note: 19,968 of these are the per-expert bank tensors, each [1024, 2304] bf16 = 4.72 MB, below the compact threshold, so the size policy widens every one of them to f32

baseline_measured.B1_shared_expert_silently_dropped: The container's graph declares `moe.shared_experts: 1` and lists 78 shared-expert tensors (26 routed layers × gate/up/down, [1024,2304]/[2304,1024] bf16, 0.37 GB) which closure counts as ACCOUNTED (layer 1: 790/790 = 768 per-expert + 22 decoder_stack tensors including the three shared ones). The plan carries NO `SharedExpertOp`: `opplan::build::shared_expert_width` returns `None` when the graph's `shared_expert_intermediate_size` is absent, and that field (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if)]`) entered the graph schema on 2026-09-03 (`9d5f9965`, semantics 9) — after every real container on disk was encoded. So the 3b refusal `SharedExpertProject → MissingRealization` never fires on a real model, and 98.25 − 97.78 = 0.47 GB of stored bytes are planned by nothing (0.37 GB of it the shared expert). The Kimi-specific loader (`exec/kimi_source.rs`) binds the same branch BY NAME outside the plan, so the two execution paths disagree about the model's operand set.
baseline_measured.B2_per_expert_bank_misclassified: `planned_operands()` lists a per-expert bank as 19,968 ordinary `Operation::Project(FfnProjection)` operands. The selector admits each as a whole projection (widen-to-f32, 188 GB), the executor cannot run any of them (`RoutedOperands::load` refuses `ExpertBank::PerExpert` at load, AFTER layer 0's bytes were read), and the residency verdict is wrong in kind: a bank is held as stored and gathered top-k per token, never widened matrix by matrix. The old three-axes refusal (94 GB bf16 → 188 GB f32) reproduces exactly, now as a declaration before I/O — which is progress in location, not in substance.
baseline_measured.B3_what_already_executes: The per-expert bank and the shared expert DO execute on CPU today — through `exec/{kimi_source,kimi_router,kimi_moe_block,kimi_kda_layer,kimi_mla_layer,stack}.rs`, with real-checkpoint oracles (`kimi_moe_real`, `kimi_kda_layer_real`, `kimi_mla_layer_real`, `generate_real` 16/16 greedy tokens) and a mapped-region loader that binds bf16 slices without copying (`ExpertWeights<'_>` over mmap'd segments). None of it passes through `PreparedOperands`, so none of it is selected, pinned, priced or reconciled. The vertical's realization work is BINDING an existing executor as a named realization, not writing kernels.
baseline_measured.B4_parity_assets: Python oracle exporters exist for every rung (scripts/kimi_{moe,kda_layer,mla_layer,two_layer,stack,generate,token}_export.py; torch 2.6.0, transformers 5.5.0 present; HF checkpoint present, 92 GB). No fixture is on disk (/tmp/kimi_* absent) — every oracle must be regenerated (minutes each). The miniature `fixtures_kimi::hybrid_kda_mla_f32_model` is consumed only by the planner's tests, never executed through the prepared plan.

design_frozen_at_the_contract_level.D1 shared expert is planned or refused,: A routed-FFN judgment with `shared_experts > 0` and no stored width resolves the width by the ONE rule the models crate already states (`ModelArchitecture::shared_expert_intermediate_size`: the declared key, else count × routed width) and VERIFIES it against the stored shapes of the three shared tensors, which the builder already checks for a declared width (`expected_shape`). A branch whose width is neither declared nor confirmed by its tensors' shapes is a closure defect and refuses the layer by name. `absent_op`/`required_roles` and the op are then paired for real. Fixtures that declare the width (Qwen-MoE shape) produce byte-identical plans.
design_frozen_at_the_contract_level.D2 a per-expert bank is its own operatio: `Operation::ExpertProject { experts, top_k }` replaces `Project(FfnProjection)` for `ExpertBank::PerExpert` operands. Operation MULTIPLICITY is preserved for execution touch (19,968 logical accesses, top_k per token), while the plan represents the SHARED PHYSICAL STORAGE: one bank object per layer per projection family, bound once, priced once for footprint and residency. Until D4 lands, the CPU selector refuses each as `MissingRealization` — the complete pre-I/O list — and the per-expert loader refusal at load becomes unreachable.
design_frozen_at_the_contract_level.D3 the budget is an input to preparation: `PreparedOperands::load` and `select_realizations` take a `ResidencyBudget` (`Machine` = physical memory, `Bytes(n)`, `Unbounded` for tests/oracles). Applied only after D1/D2/D4/D5 make the plan complete. Under a budget, selection CHOOSES among the realizations an operand has — resident (decoded/requantised in memory), mapped on-demand (the stored bank bound once, paged as touched), decoded, staged — by the declared working set they imply, and pins the executable set; when no set fits, it refuses before any payload byte with the exact deficit (declared working set, budget, the operands that break it) and the alternatives it considered. `Unbounded` reproduces today's pins byte for byte. The user's ruling supersedes the earlier 'the budget only refuses': 'all operands pinned at 178 GiB' is a diagnostic baseline, never an admitted executable plan.
design_frozen_at_the_contract_level.D4 the CPU per-expert realization binds: The EXISTING mapped Kimi executor is registered as a named realization — no new kernel: `RealizationForm::Direct(FusedBf16)` on an `ExpertProject` operand means the bank stays in its stored bf16 form, bound ONCE as mapped regions of the container's segment (the `kimi_source` binding, lifted into `LoadedWeight`/`Bound` as a mapped object so the census covers the bound buffer), gathered top-k per token, executed by `kimi_moe_block::expert_ffn`. A realization covers the BANK, not one operand: one bound object serves thousands of logical accesses. Declared residency = the bank's stored bytes; declared touch per token = top_k × 3 × expert bytes. A realization that COPIES the bank is never a candidate.
design_frozen_at_the_contract_level.D5 the shared expert executes through th: `RoutedFfnCall` gains `shared: Option<SharedExpertWeights>`; the executor composes the unscaled add (`y = moe(x) + shared(x)`, `KimiSparseMoeBlock.forward`) once, backend-independently; the three shared projections are ordinary dense projections under the size policy (4.72 MB → widened f32). Their realization records read `SharedExpertProject → Decode(BlasF32)` with reason `SizePolicy`.
design_frozen_at_the_contract_level.D6 observed residency, not declared, pri: Reconciliation extends to mapped objects: a mapped bank's OBSERVED residency is its touched pages (RSS delta / mincore over the mapping after N tokens), reported beside the declared stored bytes; direct (bf16 mapped), decoded (widened f32 dense side) and requantised (Q8 dense side) paths are priced from those observations and the ledger's per-token touch, in one table. No tok/s figure is forecast here — the K3 pre-registration's own rule: no bands until measured.
design_frozen_at_the_contract_level.D7 the parity ladder runs THROUGH the pr: one layer — layer 1 (KDA + routed + shared) via `ExecutionSlice::LayerRange{1,2}` against the Python oracle (`kimi_kda_layer_export.py --layer 1`), every boundary exposed; miniature — `hybrid_kda_mla_f32_model` through `execute_plan` under the production backend against the reference backend AND against an f32 transcription with a per-expert control (wrong expert's weights); full — 16 greedy tokens on the real container through `vindex3 generate` against `kimi_generate_export.py`'s trajectory (16/16 ids, top-10 stable), the same gate `generate_real` closed on the Kimi-specific path.

predictions.P1 after D1 on the real container: planned operands 20081 → 20159 (+78 SharedExpertProject); with D2/D4 absent the selector refuses ALL 78 as MissingRealization, before I/O, in one list; every fixture that declares a shared width plans byte-identically (plan JSON diff empty).
predictions.P2 after D2: 19,968 operands re-listed under ExpertProject{256, 8}; refused as MissingRealization until D4; the load-time PerExpert refusal is unreachable (its test moves to the selector).
predictions.P3 after D3: the baseline plan refuses at preparation with 'declared working set 179.75 GiB exceeds budget 128 GiB' naming the bank tensors first; `Unbounded` reproduces today's behaviour byte for byte.
predictions.P4 after D4+D5, declared: resident ≈ 94.22 GB (mapped bank, stored) + 1.45 GB (98 Q8 requantised dense operands, 1.36 G weights) + 1.51 GB (embedding f32 gather) + 0.74 GB (78 shared projections widened) + 0.06 GB (7 FusedBf16) ≈ 98.0 GB ≈ 91.3 GiB — WITHIN a 128 GiB budget with ≈ 37 GiB headroom; execution touch per token ≈ 2.14 GB dense (decoder_stack minus shared) + 0.75 GB head + 0.113 GB routed (8 × 3 × 4.72 MB) + 0.014 GB shared ≈ 3.0 GB stored bytes per token.
predictions.P5 observed vs declared: after 64 decode tokens the mapped bank's touched pages ≈ tokens × top_k × 3 × 4.72 MB minus overlap — well under 10 GB, i.e. the OBSERVED residency of the bank is a small fraction of its DECLARED (stored) 94 GB; this gap is the number the residency chapter wants and the reason declared-resident must not be the only column.
predictions.P6 parity: one layer: every boundary within the existing `kimi_kda_layer_real` bounds (rel-RMS ≤ 3e-4 at the layer output); miniature: production == reference to f32 summation noise, and the wrong-expert control fails by orders; full: 16/16 greedy ids, top-10 stable.
predictions.P7 the reconciliation: every pin of the real plan reconciles with a bound object — the mapped bank as ONE bound object per layer per projection family, not 19,968 allocations; mutating the bank's declared element width breaks exactly the bank rows of the reconciliation and nothing else.

review_before_freeze: User review 2026-09-05, applied before the commit that freezes this file: the codec plane has done its job — K3 fails at realization and residency, not representation. The 178 GiB figure is not to be optimised: it is produced by an incomplete, mis-modelled plan (shared expert absent, one physical bank as 19,968 whole projections, the mapped Kimi executor invisible as a realization). Semantic truth first; the budget applies only once the plan is complete; execution proof last.
acceptance_statement: The complete K3 graph selects a physically executable set of realizations within the machine budget, or refuses before reading payload bytes with the exact deficit and alternatives.
what_k3_teaches_the_lowering_contract: realizations are not always independent tensor kernels: one stored bank may serve thousands of logical operations
one object may be bound once but touched repeatedly — footprint and touch are different sums
a realization may cover a bank or a subgraph, not merely one operand
residency cannot be calculated by summing independently selected pins
graph completeness must be checked before target lowering
the next abstraction, named by the hostile real model: shared, bank-scoped execution realizations under a global residency budget
